description: Build a native DAW PROJECT from stems: each stem on its own audio track from bar 1, optional MIDI tracks (the written parts) beside them, on your tempo (bpm or tempo_map) — Logic Pro (.logicx) or Ableton Live (.als), zipped. The deliverable after doseedo_render_score (pass from_job: its job_id and the stems, MIDI and tempo come from that job) or after any renders / separations you made (stems: [{name, audio_url}] — result links work as-is). After doseedo_mix add mix_job: each track at that mix's level and pan, the mix as a muted reference track. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~30–90 s) → file (pre-signed zip, curl -o session.zip <url>, 24 h). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running session build — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

cues.description: MCP: ONE session for a whole scored film — [{cue: "1M1", start_s, from_job: <its doseedo_render_score job>, mix_job?: <its doseedo_mix job>, emotion?}] (≤ 12 cues, from the cue sheet's start_s). Every cue's stems and MIDI land on one timeline at its start, on ONE tempo map (each cue's own tempo_map joined, each cue's bar 1 on a bar line), a marker per cue, each track at its cue's mix level and pan, each cue's mix as a muted reference. Replaces from_job / mix_job / stems.

from_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_render_score job_id — its stems, parts' MIDI and tempo are used (no other input needed).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

markers.description: Arrangement markers [{name, beat}] — beat 0 = bar 1 on the project's tempo map. A scored film's cues are written as markers by `cues`.

midi_tracks.description: Optional MIDI tracks: [{name, notes:[{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity?}]}].

mix_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_mix job_id — every track takes that mix's level and pan, and the mix itself rides along as a muted reference track "Mix (doseedo)".

mixgraph.description: A mix document (doseedo_mix → mixgraph): each stem named in it takes its strip's gain_db and pan. The EQ, compression, reverb and rides are not written into the project.

name.description: Project name — the project inside the zip, and the zip itself downloads as <name>_session.zip.

session_beats.description: Length of the session in beats (the tempo map is written this far; default: the last note). `cues` sets it.

stems.description: [{name, audio_url | audio_key, gain_db?, pan?, mute?, position_beats?}] — the audio tracks, in order.

target.description: Which DAW (default logic): Logic Pro (.logicx), Ableton Live (.als) or REAPER (.rpp + media, with the film as a video track). Or a VIDEO EDITOR, for whoever cuts the picture: premiere (Premiere Pro: an FCP7 XML), finalcut (Final Cut Pro: an FCPXML) or resolve (DaVinci Resolve: both). An editor project is the film on V1, every stem as its own clip at its position (one track per part across the cues), a marker per cue, the sequence at the film's own start timecode, with its media beside it (48 kHz, 24-bit). Each stem's gain_db and pan are printed into its file, so clips sit at unity; midi_tracks and the tempo map are not written (a timeline holds none).

tempo_map.description: Tempo changes [{beat, bpm}] for the project.

video.description: The film the music is written to: {video_key: the ingest/ key of your upload (doseedo_get_upload_url), name?, start_s?}. It is re-encoded lean (720p) and travels inside the project: REAPER gets a muted video track, Logic Pro gets its Movie (inside the package; Logic finds it by name). Ableton projects are built without it (the answer says so).

name: doseedo_session_from_stems
title: Stems → a DAW session
